Reproduce and validate a dashboard chart

Mustapha Mohammed, Sarah Hamed, Souci Frissa, Aisha Mohamed and Nathan Stanley, Black Thrive Global

23 October 2026

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

BlackThriveSS makes a fixed set of public dashboard evidence available in R: a catalogue of force, council and national datasets from 2018 onwards, the dashboard’s force ranking chart for any year and group, and links that carry a chart to and from the dashboard website. The package includes all the data used in this tutorial; running it needs no network connection or dashboard session.

This tutorial covers the data and the ranking chart. Two companion vignettes go further: vignette("robustness", package = "BlackThriveSS") shows how to test what a disparity estimate rests on (bounds under unknown ethnicity, rank intervals, change with coverage), and vignette("briefing", package = "BlackThriveSS") shows how to brief one force or council, including a one-call HTML briefing.

Install and discover

BlackThriveSS is not on CRAN yet. Install the current release from GitHub with remotes::install_github("BlackThrive/BlackThriveSS"); the package itself is pure R, and on Windows and macOS the dependencies install as CRAN binaries. Start by listing what is in the box:

library(BlackThriveSS)
btg_datasets()[c("dataset", "level", "from", "to", "groups", "coverage")]
dataset level from to groups coverage
force_disparity force 2025 2025 Black TRUE
force_ethnicity_year force 2018 2026 Asian, Black, Mixed, Other TRUE
national_year national 2018 2026 FALSE
national_month_ethnicity national 2018 2026 Asian, Black, Mixed, Other, White, Unknown FALSE
council_ethnicity_year council 2018 2026 Asian, Black, Mixed, Other FALSE
hit_rate_ethnicity_year national 2018 2026 Asian, Black, Mixed, Other, White, Unknown FALSE
section60_force_year force 2018 2026 Asian, Black, Mixed, Other, White, Unknown TRUE 
btg_releases()
release source_month dashboard_built_at datasets
dashboard-2026-07-2025-99a88b69f2d6 2026-07 2026-09-16T07:12:19Z force_disparity
dashboard-2026-07-catalogue-bacf49c2a48d 2026-07 2026-09-16T07:12:19Z force_ethnicity_year, national_year, national_month_ethnicity, council_ethnicity_year, hit_rate_ethnicity_year, section60_force_year

Each row of btg_datasets() also carries the dataset’s title and the release it belongs to.

Load the evidence 

x <- btg_get_data()
x
#> BlackThriveSS: force_disparity (2025)
#> Release: dashboard-2026-07-2025-99a88b69f2d6
#> 44 rows at force level; 40 with dashboard-eligible ratios
#> Tables: $data and $coverage; provenance: $metadata
head(x$data[c("force", "ratio", "months_supplied", "coverage_status")])
force ratio months_supplied coverage_status
avon-and-somerset 7.119841 12 all_months_supplied
bedfordshire 4.451979 12 all_months_supplied
btp NA 12 all_months_supplied
cambridgeshire 7.573837 12 all_months_supplied
cheshire 6.545908 12 all_months_supplied
city-of-london NA 12 all_months_supplied

The object contains ordinary data frames in x$data and x$coverage, plus explicit metadata and selection lists. This snapshot has 44 force rows, including British Transport Police, and 528 monthly coverage entries. The dashboard display rule allows 40 force ratios. An eligible ratio does not imply that a force supplied all 12 months.

The fixed release identifies the July 2026 source archive used by the local dashboard, whose aggregates were built in September 2026. It is not a statement about the newest data available online. Specify a release when writing a reproducible analysis:

release <- btg_releases()$release[1]
met <- btg_get_data(force = "metropolitan", years = 2025, release = release)
met$data[c("black_stops", "white_stops", "black_population", "white_population", "ratio")]
black_stops white_stops black_population white_population ratio
56116 48798 1188137 4725217 4.573408

Browse the catalogue

force_disparity is the package’s original dataset. The catalogue release adds every year the dashboard holds and all four groups compared with White, plus national and council tables. Each dataset is read with the same function and verified against its checksum:

y <- btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year", groups = "Black", years = 2022:2025)
y
#> BlackThriveSS: force_ethnicity_year (2022 to 2025)
#> Release: dashboard-2026-07-catalogue-bacf49c2a48d
#> 176 rows at force level; 158 with dashboard-eligible ratios
#> Tables: $data and $coverage; provenance: $metadata
head(y$data[c("force_label", "year", "group", "ratio", "rank", "coverage_status")])
force_label year group ratio rank coverage_status
Avon and Somerset 2022 Black 5.542059 19 unverified
Bedfordshire 2022 Black 4.799220 25 unverified
British Transport Police 2022 Black NA NA unverified
Cambridgeshire 2022 Black 5.829275 13 unverified
Cheshire 2022 Black NA NA unverified
London, City of 2022 Black NA NA unverified 
btg_get_data("national_year")$data[c("year", "stops", "arrest_rate", "hit_rate")]
year stops arrest_rate hit_rate
2018 319569 15.72149 53.55583
2019 524424 12.80929 47.37039
2020 676628 11.38765 40.16794
2021 541523 12.22386 42.84181
2022 477044 12.81140 43.66568
2023 449005 13.95909 44.48123
2024 471542 15.13587 48.32125
2025 505586 14.66833 49.67239
2026 275024 15.49647 50.46486

The 2025 Black rows of force_ethnicity_year reproduce force_disparity exactly. Coverage differs by year: the dashboard verifies monthly submissions only inside a recent window, so earlier years are unverified, which is not the same as missing. The final source year is incomplete, and months_in_source says how many of its months the source month covers.

lambeth <- btg_get_data("council_ethnicity_year", council = "E09000022", years = 2025)
lambeth$data[c("group", "group_stops", "white_stops", "ratio")]
group group_stops white_stops ratio
Asian 273 1501 1.3790466
Black 4773 1501 7.2988782
Mixed 0 1501 0.0000000
Other 125 1501 0.8065571

Council counts depend on stop coordinates, which some forces do not publish, so they undercount and carry no display rule or rank.

Recreate and edit the chart 

p <- btg_plot_disparity(x)
p

The bars reproduce the dashboard ranking’s values and ordering. This static ggplot uses portable system fonts; it does not include interactive hover text or previous-year change annotations. An asterisk and a lighter fill mark partial or unverified reporting, and each bar carries its 95% interval. Counts are not annualised.

Any year and group in force_ethnicity_year can be drawn, and one force can be highlighted as the dashboard’s selected force:

btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024, group = "Asian",
                   highlight = "metropolitan")

Use ranking = "lowest" or ranking = "closest" to change the ordering and n to choose the maximum number of bars. Force subsets retain ranks from the full release. The returned plot can be styled with ordinary ggplot2 functions:

p + ggplot2::labs(title = "My local evidence briefing")
ggplot2::ggsave("disparity.png", p, width = 11.5, height = 7.5, dpi = 160)
head(btg_figure_data(p)[c("force_label", "ratio", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "coverage_status")])
force_label ratio ci_lower ci_upper coverage_status
Norfolk 9.971068 8.538263 11.644313 partial_year
Devon & Cornwall 9.748324 8.430189 11.272561 all_months_supplied
West Mercia 9.673906 8.451227 11.073475 all_months_supplied
Sussex 9.461250 8.726800 10.257511 all_months_supplied
Surrey 8.612550 7.961842 9.316438 all_months_supplied
Dorset 8.217899 6.410803 10.534385 all_months_supplied

The figure table describes the original evidence. User-added ggplot layers or styles do not alter that table or the saved evidence specification. For your own calculations, transform a copy of x$data; the reproduction functions reject modified evidence or provenance.

Check reporting coverage and consistency 

btg_coverage(met)
force force_label month status records
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-01 supplied 11634
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-02 supplied 10489
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-03 supplied 11116
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-04 supplied 10779
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-05 supplied 10688
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-06 supplied 10663
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-07 supplied 11254
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-08 supplied 14899
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-09 supplied 11151
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-10 supplied 11749
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-11 supplied 12355
metropolitan Metropolitan Police 2025-12 supplied 11861 
checks <- btg_validate(x)
checks[c("check", "passed")]
check passed
release_integrity TRUE
schema TRUE
types TRUE
keys TRUE
period TRUE
counts TRUE
missing_returns TRUE
coverage_summary TRUE
monthly_totals TRUE
ethnicity_totals TRUE
derived_estimates TRUE
rank_encoding TRUE 
stopifnot(all(checks$passed))

btg_validate() verifies release integrity and internal consistency, including monthly-to-annual totals, ethnicity subtotals and calculated rates. It does not certify that all events were recorded. A missing submission remains NA, not zero. For example, this snapshot has no 2025 returns for Greater Manchester or Gwent; their annual counts remain missing.

btg_get_data(force = c("greater-manchester", "gwent"))$data[
  c("force_label", "total_records", "months_missing", "coverage_status")]
force_label total_records months_missing coverage_status
Greater Manchester NA 12 no_months_supplied
Gwent NA 12 no_months_supplied

Save an exact evidence view 

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
btg_save_view(p, path)
recreated <- btg_from_view(path)
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(p), btg_figure_data(recreated)))
unlink(path)

Use a durable file path in your own project when you want to keep the view. The JSON pins the release, payload checksums, selected forces and chart version. The original bundled example is also installed with the package. Unknown releases or incompatible versions fail rather than substituting newer data. Custom ggplot styling is not saved. Pixel identity requires matching fonts and graphics dependencies; the evidence table is the reproducibility contract.

Round-trip with the dashboard website

The dashboard describes every view in its address. btg_dashboard_url() turns a chart into the link that opens the Disparity page at the same year, group and selected force, and btg_from_url() reproduces the chart behind a link copied from the website’s Share view button:

chart <- btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024,
                            group = "Asian", highlight = "metropolitan")
link <- btg_dashboard_url(chart)
link
#> [1] "https://bgtresearch-stop-search-dashboard.share.connect.posit.cloud/?tab=disparity&year=2024&eth=Asian&def=std&view=chart&force=Metropolitan%20Police"
back <- btg_from_url(link)
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(back), btg_figure_data(chart)))

The default link form is read by every deployed dashboard version, but it carries only the year, group, display and selected force. The format = "state" form also carries the ranking order and the source month, so a chart ordered by closeness to parity survives the trip only in that form:

closest <- btg_plot_disparity(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year"), year = 2024,
                              group = "Asian", ranking = "closest")
stopifnot(identical(btg_figure_data(btg_from_url(btg_dashboard_url(closest, format = "state"))),
                    btg_figure_data(closest)))

btg_from_url() warns when a link was made from a different source month than the snapshot. A link selects a view; the website recomputes its numbers from its current release, while the chart in R stays pinned to the snapshot. Set options(BlackThriveSS.dashboard_url = ...) to link to another deployment.

Go further

Trends, change, robustness and briefings each have one function:

btg_plot_trend(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year", force = "metropolitan"))

head(btg_sensitivity(x)[c("force_label", "ratio", "ratio_min", "ratio_max", "parity_direction")], 3)
force_label ratio ratio_min ratio_max parity_direction
Norfolk 9.971068 9.616471 13.78856 above
Devon & Cornwall 9.748324 9.336930 20.94084 above
West Mercia 9.673906 9.134508 16.13726 above 
head(btg_change(btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year", groups = "Black"))[c("force_label", "change", "change_direction")], 3)
force_label change change_direction
Avon and Somerset 1.0433035 unclear
Bedfordshire 0.9706147 unclear
British Transport Police NA NA

btg_profile() gathers all of this for one area as plain statements, and btg_report() renders it as an HTML briefing; see the briefing vignette.

Police.uk stop-and-search records and ONS Census 2021 resident populations. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. https://data.police.uk/about/ ; https://www.nomisweb.co.uk/sources/census_2021"
citation("BlackThriveSS")
#> Please cite the package and identify the data release using
#> btg_citation(x).
#> 
#>   Mohammed M, Hamed S, Frissa S, Mohamed A, Stanley N (2026).
#>   _BlackThriveSS: Reproduce Black Thrive Stop and Search Dashboard

#>

#>     title = {BlackThriveSS: Reproduce Black Thrive Stop and Search Dashboard Evidence},
#>     author = {Mustapha Mohammed and Sarah Hamed and Souci Frissa and Aisha Mohamed and Nathan Stanley},
#>     year = {2026},
#>     organization = {Black Thrive Global},
#>     note = {R package version 0.1.0},
#>     url = {https://blackthrive.github.io/BlackThriveSS/},
#>   }

The data dictionary defines every column; it is also installed with the package:

system.file("NOTES", "data-dictionary.md", package = "BlackThriveSS")

Rates divide recorded group events by Census 2021 residents. These denominators are not measured 2025 street exposure. The counts are events, not unique people; the aggregate cannot separate vehicle-only searches. Police officer-defined ethnicity differs from Census self-reported ethnicity. Approximate Poisson intervals condition on observed counts and fixed populations, and do not capture missing returns, repeat stops or classification uncertainty. A ratio is not an individual stop probability or a causal estimate of discrimination.

Common problems

  • Package not found: install the release first, and add its chosen library with .libPaths(c("/path/to/library", .libPaths())) in a fresh session.
  • Unknown force: use the exact identifiers in btg_get_data()$data$force.
  • Unsupported year: force_disparity holds 2025 only; use force_ethnicity_year for other years, within the range btg_datasets() shows.
  • Link cannot be reproduced: only Disparity page links are supported, and the expanded Black definition rests on self-defined ethnicity the package does not bundle.
  • No eligible ratios: BTP, City of London or a missing-return selection may have no displayable resident-based comparison; inspect counts and coverage.
  • Changed evidence: obtain a fresh object with btg_get_data(). Keep custom analysis in a separate data frame.
  • Unknown release or checksum mismatch: obtain the package release that carries that snapshot. Editing a view identifier would change the evidence.
